edges.label: 0x1879850 first visits the complete FamilyData spouse vector (+0x20), then its betrothed ID (+0x10), then relation-map rows (Character+0x1A8->+0x20, stride0x10). The latter excludes spouse/betrothed duplicates, requires relation+0x94 != 0 and +0x1A9 == 0, matching the established native IsAlliedTo predicate 0x2661E00.

The fourth source is military+0x248 CSubjectContract IDs: subject+0x20 qualifies only with an explicitly present tributary_war_participation_obligation whose level is not its native default. The fifth source is the root own contract+0x28 suzerain when explicitly present suzerain_war_participation_guarantee is non-default. These names are independently bound by 0x2D59578/0x2D595B1 to database+0xF18/+0xF28.

The final source resolves Character+0x1C0->+0x80 as ConfederationID and enumerates that Confederation+0x18 full CharacterID vector (count+0x24), skipping the root itself and IDs already seen. GetConfederation registration/callback/getter independently names that exact ID field.

Actor configuration enables filter_a: candidates whose military+0x318 vector count+0x0C is nonzero are excluded. IsAtWar registration 0x50CF7D -> callback 0x2622F10 -> getter 0x2610510 independently names this condition. Target configuration disables this extra filter.

Actor filter_b excludes candidates recognized by 0x28BCEB0 in the human-player CharacterID set; target configuration disables this extra filter. This affects estimated actor network contribution, not the legality of sending an actual call to war.

Actor filter_c first excludes candidates with the same valid non--1 ConfederationID. It then excludes the root native GetSuzerain result when the root own subject contract has an explicitly non-default suzerain_war_participation_guarantee. The older same-realm/government labels are not supported names for these instructions. Target configuration disables both extra exclusions.

Every admitted contributor adds military+0x308 without a percentage discount in this collector. The first sources populate a local seen vector even after common-filter rejection; later contract/confederation sources check it. This is ordered duplicate suppression across sources, not a claim that the first spouse vector is generically deduplicated by this function.

The shared filter calls 0x1B35DF0(root,candidate) and requires true before accumulation. That function constructs root scope, binds the candidate CharacterID into a named scope slot, and evaluates the singleton+0xF08 object subobject+0x1960. Its exact authored rule-name binding remains unresolved in this package.
